newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Sources say Daimler to absorb Mercedes unit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sources say Daimler to absorb Mercedes unit.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG will this month finalise long-mooted plans to merge its luxury car-making unit Mercedes-Benz into the parent group, sources close to the industrial giant told Reuters on Saturday.
The sources said Daimler's supervisory board was expected to approve a proposal for a merger to be effective from January 1 1997 at its meeting scheduled for January 23.
Daimler itself declined direct comment, merely repeating that the meeting this month would reach a final decision on Daimler's future group organisation.

There has been much speculation about the possible repercussions from Daimler's long-planned group restructure, which form part of its chief executive Juergen Schrempp's initiative to streamline the organisation.

The German media has reported repeatedly that Mercedes' highly-respected chief executive Helmut Werner threatened to leave the Daimler group because of his opposition to Schrempp's plans and might do so if the merger went ahead.
The sources did not comment on Werner but said the new management board of the restructured Daimler group would not include a post carrying responsibility for the entire Mercedes group.
The sources were confirming a report this weekend in the Spiegel magazine, which said a decision had finally been reached on the future status of Mercedes in the Daimler group.

Spiegel had said that Hilmar Kopper, the outgoing Deutsche Bank AG chief executive who heads Daimler's supervisory board, and Karl Feuerstein, head of Daimler's works council, had indicated they approved the move.

The magazine also said that Mercedes future representation on the Daimler-Benz management board would comprise representatives of its car division, its commercial division and its distribution department.
Helmut Werner's fate was not yet clear, Spiegel said.
Werner reportedly opposes a merger of Mercedes into Daimler because of his fears that the carmaker would be stripped of much of its independence by such a move.
Since Juergen Schrempp's takeover at the helm of Daimler in May 1995, the group has given up 11 of the 35 business divisions it once controlled.
